method.what: Every tracked text file outside this edition was read line by line by build/audit.py and compared with nine figures read from official pages on 2026-11-10; every external address was classed by host.
The 26 sources behind the published root portal (integration/evidence.json) were matched against the pages this session opened; 15 were re-read and their figures compared.
REQUIREMENTS.md, EXECUTIVE_SUMMARY.md, COORDINATION.md, integration/costs.json, the Edition D parameter file and the Edition D and J flag files were read directly.

findings.title: The published portal leaves every all-in cost cell blank
findings.detail: All 40 rows carry null for conversion cost, downstream charges, documentation, tax and all-in total. The portal's own evidence list already holds the Bank of China tariff note that prices full-amount delivery, and the board row that gives the conversion margin.
findings.action: This edition prices the margin, the full-amount fee and the receiving fee from official pages and publishes all-in figures for the wire route.

findings.title: The README's headline all-in figures use the lower USD 15 full-amount fee
findings.detail: README quotes USD 83.45 at USD 10,000 and USD 932.72 at USD 400,000. Edition D's parameters set the full-amount fee to USD 15. The tariff gives USD 15 only where the receiving bank keeps an account at Bank of China's New York branch, and USD 25 otherwise. That condition is not established for the US bank used as the example, so the figures may be USD 10 too low per wire.
findings.action: This edition uses USD 25 and shows the USD 15 case as a stated alternative.

findings.title: Edition D's flag on the full-amount fee is out of date
findings.detail: The flag says the USD 15 / USD 25 figures appear only in a corporate price announcement. Note 5 of Bank of China's personal price list (第三章 个人金融) states them for personal outward remittances.
findings.action: Treat the flag as resolved; keep the condition in A02.

findings.title: Editions price from {{board_n}} different rate snapshots
findings.detail: The scan found {{board_n}} distinct Bank of China USD board values across the repository, from {{board_min}} to {{board_max}} yuan per USD 100. The board read at 17:39:58 on 10 Nov 2026 shows 665.71 / 668.51, which appears nowhere else in the repository. Dollar figures in different editions are therefore not on one rate basis.
findings.action: Compare editions only after checking the board time each one states.

findings.title: {{unofficial_n}} source hosts are not official sites
findings.detail: {{unofficial_list}} are used as sources. The first is a university mirror of the US Code, the second a news agency, the third a promotion site.
findings.action: Replace with govinfo.gov or the issuing authority's own page, or mark those rows unverified.

findings.title: Edition J dates the Bank of China tariff 2014-11-01
findings.detail: That date comes from the heading of the e-banking fee table. The bank's current price list is in force from 2025-11-11 and carries the same figures.
findings.action: Cite the current price list as the dated source.

findings.title: Wise fees were left blank as quote-time only
findings.detail: Earlier editions recorded the Wise caps but no fee. Five quotes were read today for CNY 66,711 to CNY 300,000.
findings.action: Priced in this edition; the quotes are dated and flagged as time-stamped.

findings.title: Earlier editions still mention the 2021 virtual-currency notice
findings.detail: The 2026 joint notice (银发〔2026〕42号) is the current text. Edition J records the repeal; the older mentions should be read as historical.
findings.action: No change made; listed for review.

findings.title: Links to official sites over plain http
findings.detail: {{http_n}} official hosts are linked with http rather than https: {{http_list}}. The pages opened for this session, so the links work.

findings.title: {{portal_reread}} of {{portal_sources}} portal sources re-read; figures agree
findings.detail: Bank of China commission and cable fee, the HSBC China scale, Wise caps, the card-cash caps, the SAFE Hebei periods, section 988 wording, the FBAR threshold and the Form 3520 thresholds all match what was read today. Edition B's FBAR penalty figures (USD 16,536 and USD 165,353) match the current regulation.

findings.title: No statement contradicting the nine scanned figures was found
findings.detail: Where the scan found a different number on a matching line, the sampled lines were read: each was another field on the same line, for example HSBC's CNY 100 minimum beside the cable fee, or the 1–2 working days Wise quotes for verification.
findings.action: See the scan table for counts and sample locations.

findings.title: {{portal_not_reread}} portal sources were not re-opened today
findings.detail: They include the Western Union page, the Supreme Court's Bittner opinion, the 2026 dividend-tax announcement and the 2003 cash-carrying notice. They stand as verified by earlier sessions only.
